preamble: The velar fricative [x] becomes the alveolar sibilant [s] in the Slavic second (regressive) and progressive palatalizations. Before the new front vowels *ě and *i that arose from the diphthongs *ai and *oi, and after front vowels in the progressive palatalization, Proto-Slavic *x was fronted to a palatal sibilant *ś, which then merged with *s in East and South Slavic (and in Slovak) but with *š in the rest of West Slavic. The attested outcome in Old Church Slavonic and Russian is plain [s], producing alternations such as OCS доухъ 'spirit' beside nominative plural доуси. Old Novgorodian, which escaped the progressive palatalization, preserves the original velar.

examples.to: доуси (dusi) nom. pl., доусѣ (dusě) loc. sg.
examples.note: Second palatalization: *x before *i and *ě from earlier *oi and *ai gives s, producing a regular x ~ s alternation within the o-stem paradigm.

examples.from: Early Proto-Slavic *vьxь 'all' (cf. Old Novgorodian вьхе, without palatalization)
examples.note: Progressive palatalization: *x after the front vowel *ь became a sibilant, which surfaces as s in Old Church Slavonic.

examples.from: Early Proto-Slavic *vьxь 'all' (Old Novgorodian вьхе keeps x)
examples.note: The standard East Slavic outcome of the progressive palatalization of *x is s; the Old Novgorodian form shows the unpalatalized velar.
Slovak matches South Slavic in giving s from the second palatalization of *x, whereas Czech and Polish have š (cf. Czech Češi).
